'''''Linaria algarviana''''', commonly known as the '''Algarve toadflax''' (Portuguese: ''pombinhas-do-Algarve''), is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Plantaginaceae]], [[Endemism|endemic]] to the [[Algarve]] region of southern [[Portugal]]. It was first described by the Swiss botanist [[Édouard-Louis Chavannes]] in 1833.<ref name="iucn">{{cite web |title=Linaria algarviana |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/162054/5543821 |publisher=[[IUCN Red List of Threatened Species]] |author=Caldas, F.B. |date=2011 |access-date=19 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Linaria algarviana Chav. |url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/29205021 |website=Tropicos |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Linaria algarviana'' is an [[annual plant|annual]] herb reaching heights of {{convert|14|–|25|cm|0}}. It typically produces 1–15 stems, which are usually simple or slightly branched. The leaves are glaucous and fleshy; lower leaves are arranged in [[Whorl (botany)|whorls]], while the upper leaves are alternate and oblong-lanceolate in shape.<ref name="iberica">{{Cite book |last1=Sáez |first1=L. |last2=Bernal |first2=M. |title=Flora Iberica |publisher=Real Jardín Botánico (CSIC) |year=2009 |isbn=978-84-00-08747-0 |volume=XIII |pages=289–293 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

The [[inflorescence]] is a loose [[raceme]] of 1–8 flowers. The [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]] is 16–25 mm long and distinctly violet, featuring a yellow or beige palate (the "lower lip" bulge) marked with violet veins and spots. The nectar [[Spur (botany)|spur]] is relatively long and straight or slightly curved.<ref name="iberica" /><ref name="flora">{{cite web |title=Linaria algarviana |url=https://flora-on.pt/?q=Linaria+algarviana |website=Flora-on |publisher=Sociedade Portuguesa de Botânica |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref><ref name="Thorogood">{{cite book |last=Thorogood |first=Chris |title=Field guide to the wild flowers of the western Mediterranean |publisher=Kew publishing Royal Botanic Gardens |publication-place=Richmond |date=2016 |isbn=978-1-84246-616-2 |pages=474–475}}</ref>

The species is very similar to ''[[Linaria amethystea]]'', differing in the looser, less stiffly erect stems, and in the finely ridged seeds lacking a wing.<ref name="Thorogood"/>

=== Leaves ===
The leaves are somewhat fleshy in consistency. The lower leaves are arranged in [[Whorl (botany)|whorls]] of three or four and are oblong-lanceolate. The upper leaves are alternate, linear-lanceolate, and measure approximately 5–15 mm in length and 1–3 mm in width.<ref name="flora" />

=== Flowers ===
The inflorescence is a [[raceme]] that is initially dense but becomes lax as it elongates. The flowers are distinctly zygomorphic.
* '''Corolla:''' The corolla is 17–25 mm long and predominantly violet. It features a prominent pale yellow spot at the throat grading to a creamy-white to pinkish-white palate (the bulge at the throat) that is strikingly marked with dark violet veins and spots.
* '''Spur:''' The nectar [[Spur (botany)|spur]] is 9–13 mm long, slender, and usually straight or only slightly curved.

=== Fruit and seeds ===
The fruit is a subglobose [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] measuring 4–6 mm, which opens via apical pores (porocidal). The seeds are small (0.5–0.8 mm), black, and lack the membranous wing found in some other ''Linaria'' species; instead, they are covered in fine longitudinal ridges or crests.<ref name="iberica" /><ref name="flora" />

== Phenology ==
''Linaria algarviana'' typically flowers from February to May, with the peak flowering period occurring in March and April. Seed dispersal occurs shortly after the capsules mature in late spring.<ref name="flora" />

== Distribution and habitat ==

This species is native and restricted to the western [[Algarve]] (the ''Barlavento''), primarily between [[Lagos, Portugal|Lagos]] and the [[Sagres Point|Sagres]] peninsula. It inhabits clearings of [[Xerophyte|xerophilic]] scrubland, coastal pastures, and sandy meadows. It is occasionally found in open pine forests and vineyards, almost exclusively on shale or sandy substrates near the coastline.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /><ref name="flora" /><ref name="Thorogood"/>

== Conservation ==

Previously considered by the IUCN Red List as a species of Least Concern, it is currently evaluated as [[Near Threatened]] on the [[IUCN Red List]]. While it remains locally abundant in some areas, its restricted range makes it vulnerable to habitat loss from tourism development and agricultural intensification.<ref name="flora" /><ref name="iucn" /> 

In Portugal, it is listed on the Red List of Vascular Flora of Mainland Portugal.<ref name="vascular">{{Cite web |title=Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental |url=https://listavermelha-flora.pt/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |publisher=Sociedade Portuguesa de Botânica}}</ref> It is a protected species under the [[European Union]]'s [[Habitats Directive]] (Annexes II and IV) and the [[Berne Convention]] (Annex I).<ref name=":Habitats">{{Cite web|url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:31992L0043 |title=Council Directive 92/43/EEC |website=Eur-Lex |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref>
